It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A MAN who attacked his former partner at a Powys campsite in a jealous rage has been jailed for nearly 3 years. Shane Jones, 37, assaulted his ex-partner at the Talybont Farm Campsite in the Brecon Beacons on April 20, 2024, occasioning her actual bodily harm (ABH). He committed a further ABH assault and also strangled her during an incident at the Dyffryn Newydd Hotel in Aberbargoed, near Merthyr Tydfil, on June 16, 2024, when the couple had been out celebrating his birthday. Cardiff Crown Court heard on Thursday, August 6, that during the June 2024 ordeal, Jones choked his victim until she was unconscious. Prosecutor Paul Hewwitt said Jones initially denied all charges, before entering guilty pleas to three a week before his trial. While staying in the Brecon Beacons on April 20, an argument ensued after the couple arrived in Powys. “The argument was about a ‘like’ she’d received from a male on social media,” said Mr Hewwitt. “The defendant was jealous of any male contact. She left and went to a nearby pub. While there he sent texts calling her a ‘rat’. “He came to the pub and continued the abuse, which raised attention, and other men told him to stop. “The victim went back to the caravan and when he came back, he punched her to the face, he struck her left eye socket." As the attack continued the victim was left cowering and asking why he was hitting her, the court heard. “She phoned in sick at work the following Monday, she said she’d fallen from the caravan, but her colleagues didn’t believe her and phoned the police,” he added. Read more Welshpool duo who exploited victims' trust to steal thousands could leave jail soon Ex-Powys nurse was in 'downward spiral' after losing both parents Powys man waged 22-day campaign of verbal and physical abuse Mr Hewwitt said the June incident unfolded after Jones found his partner going through his phone. “It was his birthday; she’d bought him presents and wore new dress for the occasion,” he said. “His aggression was known to be even worse when drinking, and he’d drunk 10 pints of Madri and six Jagerbombs, before he was later sick when they got home. “The complainant, having been accused of infidelity, wondered whether he’d been cheating on her. She took his phone. “She was sitting on the toilet scrolling. He was furious and dragged her by her hair from the toilet. While staying in the Brecon Beacons on April 20, an argument ensued shortly after the couple arrived in Powys. (Image: None) “He dragged her to the bed, punched her in the face and chest, then dragged her to the floor and ripped her dress." “He placed his hands round her neck and squeezed. She became unconscious. She woke later in the bathroom, to the defendant splashing water on her face. She then fled the house and locked herself in the car. Jones has seven previous convictions, including for domestic abuse-related violence. Representing Jones, of Sycamore Court , Bargoed, Kevin Seal said his client had not committed any violent or domestic-related offences for 15 years before these incidents. “His record does not do him any favours,” said Mr Seal. “When he was very young he had difficulties. He managed for 15 years to stay out of trouble, but then he goes through a period in his life where everything seemed to go wrong." Helplines If you, or someone you know, have been affected by domestic abuse or violence, the following organisations may be able to help. If you are in immediate danger, you should dial 999. Montgomeryshire Family Crisis Centre (MFCC) on 01686 629114 Calan DVS (Mid and South Powys) on 01874 625146 Women's Aid on 0808 8010800 Polish Domestic Violence Helpline on 0800 061 4004 Recorder Claire Pickthall told Jones: “It was clear you could not accept her having male friends or colleagues. “During the June 16 assault she thought you were going to kill her. In a previous pre-sentence report you failed to accept any responsibility and said she was playing up to it. “You cannot continue to blame your childhood for your behaviour.” She jailed Jones for 34 months for the strangulation offence. Terms of 20 months and 11 months were handed down for the two ABH offences, but will be served concurrently. He must abide by a restraining order, preventing him from having any contact with the victim, for 10 years. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c68x.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Smoke billows from Yandex's Sasovo hub following a Ukrainian strike on Thursday By Tinshui Yeung Published 9 October 2026 Russian tech giant Yandex has said it was struggling to maintain services after two of its five data centres were struck by Ukrainian drones in the past two days. Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the company runs the country's most popular search engine, as well as a food-ordering and taxi app used by tens of millions of people. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks were in response to weeks of Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres. Both sides have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months as the war between the two drags on. Kyiv says its strikes are aimed at revenue streams for Moscow's war machine, and that the latest attacks could force Russia to divert resources to Yandex. Yandex said that its data centre in Sasovo, in the Ryazan region, had been "seriously damaged as a result of a drone attack" overnight into Thursday, with its operations "completely suspended". Another data centre in Kaluga, a region south-west of Moscow, had also been attacked on Friday morning, it said, with part of that site's infrastructure "taken out of service". Yandex said on Friday that its data centres were "critical" for the normal operation of its services and that it was "very difficult to predict" when they would be back online. It said teams were working "day and night" to keep services running, but "unfortunately it is not a simple task". The tech giant said none of its employees had been injured in the strikes. The regional governor in Kaluga said nine people had been injured in a drone attack on the city's infrastructure. The exact scope of the disruption to the company's services is unclear - though it told state news agency Tass that some of its AI chatbot functions were temporarily unavailable, while its smart home devices may also experience problems. Yandex previously said its Kaluga data centre was one of Russia's largest - covering an area of 130,000 sqm (1,399,000 sq ft) and consuming as much electricity annually as 220,000 UK households. Its data centre in Sasovo, meanwhile, houses two of three supercomputers used to develop the company's AI model. It is unclear whether the supercomputers survived the attack. Ukraine's defence ministry confirmed the data centre attacks, saying they could "force Russia to divert resources to repair the damaged capacity". Zelensky said Kyiv was responding to similar Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres in a "mirror-like fashion". Last month, a Russian drone hit a business centre in Kyiv , killing four people and damaging a data centre. Due to the strikes, about 100,000 households in Kyiv and the region suffered internet outages. Some Ukrainian firms have already begun moving data from damaged servers to facilities abroad. Moscow has justified the attacks by saying the data centres were used by Ukrainian military intelligence. But Ukraine accuses it of deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. Russia has stepped up strikes on energy infrastructure ahead of the winter, as it has done in previous years of the full-scale invasion, which began in 2022. Image: Florence Lo/REUTERS Advertisement North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in China via the newly opened bridge, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency reported on Saturday. "It appears that Kim Jong Un has arrived in Dandong, China, via the New Yalu River Bridge," the unnamed source said. The four-lane bridge was completed in 2014 but remained unused for 12 years due to a lack of connecting roads and customs facilities on the North Korean side. It officially opened about a week ago , marking a step towards strengthening economic ties between the neighbouring countries. China is North Korea’s largest trading partner and a key source of diplomatic, economic and political support for the isolated, nuclear-armed state, although relations between the two have not always been smooth. Kim’s trip coincides with key dates in China Neither Beijing nor Pyongyang has confirmed Kim’s visit. The trip coincides with the anniversary of China’s entry into the Korean War, known in China as the "War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea." It remains unclear whether Kim will attend commemorative events. During the 1950-53 war, Chinese troops fought alongside North Korea against South Korea and US-led United Nations forces. Kim’s visit also comes ahead of a key political meeting in Beijing on Monday, when Chinese President Xi Jinping and other senior officials gather for the fifth plenary session of the Communist Party’s powerful Central Committee. Xi visited Pyongyang in June 2019, the first visit by a Chinese leader in 14 years (File image) Image: Ahn Young-joon/AP Photo/picture alliance Bridge highlights North Korea's ties with China The New Yalu River Bridge opened just over a month after North Korea and Russia inaugurated their first road bridge , which Pyongyang hailed as a sign of closer ties. While North Korea’s trade with Russia largely involves military supplies, trade with China could provide goods needed to develop its civilian economy, analysts say.
